flawed_step: Step 3: Inferring that a frontier node n on a cheaper path has f(n)=g(n)+h(n) no greater than the cost of the popped goal. This requires an admissibility bound on h(n), which non-negativity and h(goal)=0 do not provide.
counterexample: Let edges be S→G of cost 10, S→A of cost 1, and A→G of cost 1. Set h(S)=0, h(A)=100, and h(G)=0. After expanding S, A* has G with f=10 and A with f=101, so it pops G and returns cost 10, although S→A→G costs 2.
assessment_summary: The standard A* optimality proof fails when it needs to bound the f-value of a node on an optimal path. An overestimating heuristic can postpone that node until after a suboptimal goal is popped.
